title: Factors and Multiples Worksheets: Prime and Composite Numbers
intro: Use factor pairs to distinguish prime and composite numbers.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Build arrays or list factor pairs systematically. Then connect multiplication facts to tests for multiples.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

12 = 1 × 12 = 2 × 6 = 3 × 4

A factor pair other than one times the number proves that the number is composite. To call a number prime, check that no such pair exists.

Ask your student

How many positive factors does a prime number have?

If your student needs help

If the student calls one prime, compare its single positive factor with the definition.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each sheet contains three prime-or-composite questions and three multiple checks. Numbers to classify or test range from 2 through 100. Multiple checks use divisors from 2 through 9.
